properties.tablet_comments: The text refers to the year -424/3, i.e. Artaxerxes I year 40. The left side of each monthly paragraph contains the 'Lunar Three' (Sachs, JCS 2, 278; note that instead of KUR the term UD.NÁ.A is used here), the right side lists the dates of various planetary phases, one solstice, one equinox, and a rising of Sirius. The three items last mentioned are 1 day later than the dates produced by the scheme described in HAMA 362-364.

properties.tablet_comments: Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury for years 41 and 42 of Artaxerxes II.
properties.text_comments: 6: "acronychal rising" error for "last appearance". 10: Venus did indeed pass closely below η Tauri on XII 3 of year 41 of Artaxerxes II. The next statement is unusual: planets are sometimes said to enter a constellation, but not vice versa. Venus came into the vicinity of β Tauri around this date, but did not reach the star. I do not know what part of Taurus might be restored in the beginning of the line. 14: The remark in the beginning of the line could be restored according to line 16, but there is less space here. 15: ina UD seems to stand for ina NIM. The appearances in the west were probably not observed, so no constellation is given. 16: The last five signs of this line are obscure to me. NIM DIB, if read correctly, reminds one of statements about position, but the text does not fit this interpretation. The sign read LUḪ also occurs at the beginning of line 18. One expects comments on the first appearance. 18: the first sign of this line is the same as the fifth from the right in line 16. It may be LUḪ, but I do not understand it. Whatever its meaning, the following ina 17 seems to be an "ideal" date. The next number "28" does not agree with computation (the other dates for Mercury in this text fit quite well); maybe it is to be read u 18, "or the 18th". If this is correct, the month name ZÍZ has to be restored in front of ina 17; note that a month was also left out in line 13. This still does not solve the problem of the first sign in this line.

properties.museum_no: A 3405 (in the Tablet Collection of the Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago)
properties.tablet_comments: Planetary phases ("Greek-Letter phenomena") for SE 60-70. The terminology of this text is highly abbreviated and differs from the Babylon conventions (note ABSIN0 = KI).
properties.text_comments: Some phenomena have been restored in the translation only. Because of the chronological arrangement of the text, such restorations are certain even if just the name of a planet is actually preserved. I 1´: there is a little blanc space before the damaged number, which indicates that the line was indented, as the scribe does with eclipses. A lunar eclipse did take place in SE 60 III = -251 June 21. 17´f.: lunar eclipse of -251 Dec 14. 26´: this line should concern Venus, but the traces are not clear. II 1´f.: lunar eclipse of -250 Dec 4. 17´f.: lunar eclipse of -249 May 30. 21´: instead of 28, a reading 18 is possible. VI 1´: indentation indicates a lunar eclipse; it occurred on -243 Jan 26. VII 1´f.: lunar eclipse of -243 Jul 21. 17´f.: lunar eclipse of -242 Jan 15.
